This implies that Quinidine may indirectly influence Cyp2b6 through its role in modulating the activity of its inhibitors. The lowest common ancestor of Quinidine and Ritonavir places them within the broader category of Anti-Infective Agents and Organonitrogen Compounds, suggesting a possible pharmacological mechanism involving enzyme inhibition. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible dependency on Cyp2b6, though the exact mechanism remains unclear. The evidence supports a functional link between Quinidine and Cyp2b6, but further investigation is needed to confirm the direct interaction.
